terra.problem: The verse says conceit keeps him from detecting or hating his own sin, not that he cannot look at anything else.
Saying the problem has nothing to do with what he was taught goes beyond the verse. David does not address his instruction.
The verse does not say whether anyone is hiding the man's sin from him.
The verse calls his words wicked and deceitful; it does not say that nothing he says can be trusted.
The verse says he plots on his bed but does not say it is at night.
The verse does not say he is plotting while everyone else is winding down.
The explanation is flat and repeats that he plots on his bed without much of Papa Dorin's personality.
David says the man sets himself on the path, but the text does not say nobody pushed him onto it.
Saying the path is real risks treating David's picture as a literal road. The verse also does not say he fails to reject evil only after he is on it.
The claim that other psalms speak to the soul needs a reference.
The explanation simply repeats the verse and confirms the answer. It is generic and lacks Papa Dorin's voice.
The claim that a rock is a refuge picture elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
The claim that a fountain does not run dry adds a quality David does not give the fountain of life.
First Kings 1:33 names Gihon but does not itself identify it as a spring near Jerusalem. The added details need a supporting reference.
The passage does not establish that David would never pray for people who forget God; it only gives his prayer here.
The explanation is generic and mostly repeats the answer without adding Papa Dorin's personality.
The text does not state that David fears being driven away or that he is not worried about losing a title.
Calling being driven away David's worry assigns him a feeling the text does not state.
